speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Prime Minister whether the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) restrictions can be relaxed to allow borrowers to obtain credit facilities if they are able to offer unencumbered private property as collateral to financial institutions, even if they have breached the TDSR limits, so as to enable them to manage their overall loan commitments.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This is to help ensure that borrowers have sufficient cash income to meet their debt obligations.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Even with unencumbered private property as collateral, it is important that the borrower has sufficient cash income to meet the debt obligation.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: If the borrower fails to make repayment and defaults, the lender could seize and sell the property.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This may not be a big problem for a wealthy borrower with several properties, but for someone who is living in that property, it can cause significant hardship.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I kind of expected that answer, but the reason I am highlighting it is because, as the Minister mentioned, the TDSR formula is actually focused on income and does not take into account the assets that the potential borrower may have.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We are seeing residents of ours in this current economic climate who have seen a drop in their income.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: They do believe that with the assets that they have, if there can be some relaxation where they can get a loan from a financial institution, they will be able to manage their overall indebtedness.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Of course, in their view, the bank would be secured with their asset but they feel that they have other resources to manage such a loan.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: They need to manage their current liquidity challenges.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I think this is a problem that MAS could look into.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We also have situations where retirees who are reasonably rich are unable to get any loans at all because they have no income.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think there is some leeway for this group.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, there is another group that is also, in a way, catered to.
